dedupe_keys.name: resiflow hazard agnostic transport resilience model

description: ResiFlow is a Python road and freight resilience workflow derived from the National Infrastructure Resilience Demonstrator. Its README documents baseline traffic assignment, hazard disruption, direct damage and rerouting or recovery, with separate passenger and freight origin-destination demand. Users provide a road network, OD tables, hazard-linked disruption inputs and configuration; outputs include route shifts, damage and recovery comparisons. The repository includes Sioux Falls and toy testbeds that run without the larger CONUS data bundle. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing for this code. A limitation is that the main continental application needs external input files, and the README marks one multihazard feature branch as work in progress; this draft covers the published main branch. The model can examine how road closures interrupt freight and passenger service. A first-review NIRD draft covers the upstream framework, but ResiFlow's hazard-agnostic link contract and testbeds form a distinct implementation. No road dataset or package was downloaded.
inputs: Road network, passenger and freight OD, hazard disruption and damage settings
name: ResiFlow hazard-agnostic transport resilience model
notes: G7 G7-1996. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. A pending first-review NIRD parent draft was checked; this fork adds distinct hazard and freight workflow, and the in-progress feature branch was not drafted.
outputs: Baseline and disrupted assignment, rerouting, damage and recovery comparisons
